papers.title: A Comprehensive Review of Digital Product Passports in Sustainable Manufacturing: Current State, Challenges, and Future Directions
papers.key_contribution: A review of 225 peer-reviewed studies that codes each study on more than twenty attributes. It finds mostly conceptual work, little empirical validation, and a pointer toward hybrid architectures in practice. It ends with a lifecycle framework based on inheriting information from components and processes to products.
papers.classification_scheme: Attribute grid with more than twenty attributes. The groups named in the abstract are: study type, sector, data and information modelling, architecture, technology stack, governance, scalability, and sustainability impact. The abstract does not list the classes inside each group. The review reports that blockchain is the most proposed enabler, that modelling practice is fragmented, and that open standards (AAS, RDF/OWL, sector schemas) and hybrid architectures are the stated priorities. Class lists were not read.
papers.conformance_relevance: Supplies a ready attribute list for the engine's system-profile (ICS) design, so that each claimed method family maps to a check family. Confirms that few papers validate real systems, which is the gap a black-box engine fills. Existing checks: none apply to the review itself; ICS fields would route to data.jsonschema, aas.validate, integrity.jws. New capability: none; reuse the attribute groups as ICS vocabulary after reading the full text.
papers.notes: OA link taken from OpenAlex; the Springer host needs a cookie handshake, so the full text was not read.

papers.title: Digital Product Passports: A Systematic Literature Review on Framework Design and Validation
papers.key_contribution: A systematic review (Scopus and IEEE Xplore) of studies that define, structure, or assess DPP frameworks. It rates how far each design is elaborated and how well it is validated, and it names recurring framework archetypes. Most frameworks are conceptual and validation is limited to illustrations, stakeholder opinion, or prototypes.
papers.classification_scheme: Two axes: (1) framework design elaboration and (2) validation maturity. Design archetypes named in the abstract: data-centric, layered, technology-anchored, and ecosystem-oriented. Enabling technologies that recur: digital twins, blockchain, data spaces, knowledge graphs. Validation types named: illustrative case study, stakeholder-informed assessment, prototype. Gaps named: empirical validation, cross-organisational testing, lifecycle-spanning evaluation, data governance roles, convergence on shared reference architectures, sector adaptation.
papers.conformance_relevance: Strongest evidence in the corpus that cross-organisational, black-box testing of DPP systems is missing. The validation-maturity scale can label engine evidence levels (illustration, prototype, tested against a pinned contract). Existing checks: none applies to the paper; the maturity scale maps to the recording and replay evidence model. New capability: none; use as justification and as a vocabulary.
papers.notes: MDPI blocks WebFetch; abstract only.

papers.title: Enabling a dynamic information flow in digital product passports during product use phase: A literature review and proposed framework
papers.key_contribution: Reviews 25 DPP frameworks across industries and finds that QR codes and RFID tags are the usual carriers and blockchain the usual security solution. It notes that little work lets third-party service providers such as repairers update a passport during use, and it proposes a blockchain-based framework for verified updates.
papers.classification_scheme: Four review areas: data carrier, data source, data security, and user access and verification. Stored information is also sorted into four lifecycle stages. Observed classes: carriers (QR code, RFID tag), security approach (blockchain most common). The use-phase update path for third-party service providers is the gap.
papers.conformance_relevance: The four areas map directly onto engine test families: carrier (carrier.qr_decode), source and update path (persistence.versions), security (integrity.jws), access (access.restricted_fields). Use-phase third-party updates are a write path that no existing check exercises. New capability: an authorized active write-path test (would need a signed authorization scope).
papers.notes: Crossref lists the first author as Paul Keng Fai Wan; Consensus lists P. Wan; OpenAlex lists Paul Kengfai Wan.

papers.title: Digital Product Passport (DPP) technological advancement and adoption framework: A systematic literature review
papers.key_contribution: A systematic review of technology developments and their adoption for DPPs in the circular economy. It offers a conceptual model with three parts: a technical architecture, an adoption framework, and an adoption ecosystem.
papers.classification_scheme: Three-part conceptual model: technical architecture of DPPs, adoption framework, and adoption ecosystem. The abstract gives no finer classes.
papers.conformance_relevance: Low direct value. It shows that adoption and ecosystem factors are treated apart from the technical architecture, so a conformance report should keep technical findings separate from organizational ones. Existing check: manual.review for non-technical claims. New capability: none.

papers.title: Digital Product Passport: A Review and Research Agenda
papers.key_contribution: A concept-centric systematic review with a bibliometric analysis of 40 publications since 2021. It collects guidelines on DPP structure, technology, requirements and adoption challenges, and sets a research agenda.
papers.classification_scheme: Concept-centric coding of 40 publications into four topic groups named in the abstract: structure, technology, requirements, challenges for adoption. No finer classes in the abstract.
papers.conformance_relevance: An early map of the field. Useful only to confirm that requirement catalogues were still fragmented in 2024. Existing check: none. New capability: none.

papers.title: Digital product passports
papers.key_contribution: A fundamentals paper built on a multivocal literature review. It separates the DPP from neighbouring concepts, defines it, builds a conceptual framework, and shows a scenario that instantiates the framework. It stresses that the design space is large and ambiguous.
papers.classification_scheme: A conceptual framework of building blocks and design options derived from academic and grey literature. The abstract does not list the blocks. Not read in full: the Springer page needs a cookie handshake.
papers.conformance_relevance: Frames the DPP as an inter-organizational artifact with many design options. Supports an ICS that declares design choices instead of assuming one architecture. Existing check: none. New capability: none.
papers.notes: Same record also appears in Fraunhofer and Stuttgart repositories under other DOIs (10.24406/publica-7886, 10.18419/opus-18069).

papers.title: Data Governance for Compliance with the European Digital Product Passport: a Systematic Literature Review
papers.key_contribution: A PRISMA review that compares three governance approaches (data trusts, data cooperatives, blockchain-based governance) against four DPP requirements. It states that no product category has a fully deployed DPP yet and works at the cross-sector level.
papers.classification_scheme: Governance model classes: data trust, data cooperative, blockchain-based governance. Evaluation criteria: interoperability, security, data owner control, competitiveness.
papers.conformance_relevance: Its four criteria are a compact requirement set. Interoperability and security are testable from outside; owner control and competitiveness are organizational and need manual.review. Existing checks: integrity.jws, access.restricted_fields, manual.review. New capability: none.

papers.title: The anatomy of a passport for the circular economy: a conceptual definition, vision and structured literature review
papers.key_contribution: Shows that passport variants (product, material, resource, recycling, cradle-to-cradle) share goals and traits, and defines the concept as a digital interface to a certified identity of one identifiable product and its linked lifecycle registrations. The definition is meant to ground later requirement and architecture work.
papers.classification_scheme: Terminology clustering: it groups the many passport names by shared characteristics and conceptual boundaries, and derives one definition with components, variables, and relationships. Class names beyond the passport variants listed are not in the abstract.
papers.conformance_relevance: Gives the engine a defensible term set for the glossary (passport, identity, lifecycle registration). The idea of a certified identity bound to one identifiable product matches the engine's identifier.consistency check. Existing check: identifier.consistency. New capability: none.
papers.notes: SciSpace marks it open access; link not tested.

papers.title: Digital product passports as enablers of digital circular economy: a framework based on technological perspective
papers.key_contribution: Proposes a circular-economy framework with integrated DPP characteristics and backs it with a systematic review that takes a technology view. It states that technical requirements for DPPs were still unclear.
papers.classification_scheme: Technology-oriented grouping of implementation approaches from the review, inside a generic framework adaptable per sector stage. The abstract names no classes.
papers.conformance_relevance: Marginal. It confirms that technical requirements were not settled in 2024, which supports pinning requirements to open specifications. Existing check: none. New capability: none.

papers.title: Under The Industrial Hood: A Taxonomy for Digital Product Passports
papers.first_author: Ahmad Iqbal Bin Mohd Shahir Shamsir
papers.venue: INFORMATIK 2025, Lecture Notes in Informatics (Gesellschaft für Informatik)
papers.key_contribution: A morphological taxonomy of DPP implementations built by the Nickerson method from 32 academic papers and 50 real-world cases. Three iterations (conceptual to empirical, empirical to conceptual) gave 21 dimensions in four meta-dimensions. Two experts checked it, and it is demonstrated on two real cases (a fashion group and a service provider).
papers.classification_scheme: 21 dimensions in four meta-dimensions; characteristics inside a dimension are not mutually exclusive. (1) Organization: actor type (service provider or economic operator). (2) Industrial applications: sector (automotive, electronics, fashion and textiles, food and drinks, luxury goods, battery, plastics, cross-industry); supply chain stage (raw material sourcing, manufacturing, distribution, retail or consumer use, end-of-life or second life); certifications (CE, RoHS, REACH, GOTS, an ISO standard, the EU battery regulation); geographical reach (regional, national, global); customer type (B2B, B2C); market positioning (mass market, high end). (3) Technology usage: deployment model (cloud, hybrid, on-premises); data modelling (AAS, none specified, other); blockchain (public, hybrid, private, none); IoT use; AI use; API integration (standardized or custom); encryption and authentication (distributed ledger, public key infrastructure, zero-knowledge proofs, none); product identification (serial number, QR code, RFID, NFC, GS1); security measures (tamper-proof detection, digital watermarks, none). (4) Data types: material data (raw material origins, bill of materials, hazardous substances); manufacturing data (origin or factory information, event sourcing, production batch or lot); environmental impact (carbon footprint, water usage, energy share, product emissions); usage and maintenance (user manual, maintenance guidelines, repair logs); end-of-life and second-life information (recycling guidelines, take-back and resale, disposal methods). Other technology classes: IoT use (sensor-based, real-time monitoring, smart devices, none); AI use (predictive analytics, anomaly detection, automation, none).
papers.conformance_relevance: Best candidate for the engine's ICS vocabulary: the technology-usage meta-dimension lists exactly the declarable choices (deployment, data model, identification, authentication, security) that decide which checks apply. Mapping: product identification to carrier.qr_decode and identifier.parse; data modelling AAS to aas.validate; encryption and authentication to integrity.jws; API integration standardized to api.contract; data types to data.rules. NFC, RFID, DLT, and ZKP classes have no executable check (carrier.nfc, carrier.rfid, integrity.cose are interface_only). New capability: a ledger or ZKP evidence verifier would be needed for those classes.
papers.notes: Full text read from the open GI repository PDF. First author differs by tool: Consensus lists Johanna Paeplow, SciSpace lists Frederik Möller only, OpenAlex and the PDF list Ahmad Iqbal Bin Mohd Shahir Shamsir first, then Paeplow, then Möller. Crossref returned HTTP 404 (DataCite-style DOI). The paper states that cases were found with an AI search engine; coverage of the 50 cases is therefore not reproducible.

papers.title: A Review on Digital Product Passports as Drivers of Digital Transformation in Industry
papers.venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology, and Innovation (ICE/ITMC)
papers.key_contribution: A review that proposes a taxonomy of DPP types by technology and function, an evaluation framework with metrics, and a discussion of interoperability, standardization and readiness gaps.
papers.classification_scheme: Taxonomy of DPP types on two axes, technology and function, shown as a figure and a comparison table. The abstract also announces an evaluation framework with metrics. The classes themselves were not read.
papers.conformance_relevance: An evaluation framework with metrics could seed engine acceptance criteria, but the content is unread. Existing check: none. New capability: none until the full text is read.
papers.notes: IEEE paywall; abstract only.

papers.title: A Maturity Model for Digital Product Passports: A Design Science Study
papers.key_contribution: A validated maturity model with nine technological and organizational maturation paths that firms follow to launch and run DPPs. It comes from a multivocal literature review refined in two interview series, and it notes that DPP designs show equifinality.
papers.classification_scheme: Nine maturation paths (technological and organizational) with staged levels. The abstract does not name the paths.
papers.conformance_relevance: Organizational maturity cannot be observed from outside; only a signed manual step can attest it. Existing check: manual.review. New capability: none.

papers.title: Exploring the Design Space and Research Directions for Digital Product Passport Systems
papers.venue: 2025 21st International Conference on Network and Service Management (CNSM)
papers.key_contribution: Names three technical dimensions of a DPP system (data carrier, online storage of product information, updating of dynamic data). For each, it explores architectural options and challenges and then proposes research directions. It highlights counterfeiting, interoperability, and data sovereignty, and calls for work on decentralized identity and fine-grained access management.
papers.classification_scheme: Three design-space dimensions: (1) data carrier, (2) online storage for product information, (3) updating dynamic data. Per dimension: architectural options, technical challenges, research directions. Cross-cutting challenges: counterfeiting, interoperability, data sovereignty. The class lists inside each dimension were not read; the paper is not open access.
papers.conformance_relevance: The three dimensions are the cleanest decomposition of a DPP system into testable surfaces: carrier (carrier.qr_decode; NFC and RFID are interface_only), storage and access path (identifier.resolve, api.contract, access.restricted_fields), and update path (persistence.versions, integrity.jws). Counterfeiting resistance is outside what digital consistency can prove, as the engine already states. New capability: carrier.nfc and carrier.rfid tag campaigns; an active write-path test.
papers.notes: OpenAlex gives Stefan Käser (with umlaut); Crossref gives Stefan Kaser. Authors per OpenAlex: Käser, Lesjak, Matischek, Steger. OpenAlex reports is_oa false.

papers.title: Digital Product Passport in support of Data-Driven End-of-Use Strategies–a systems design perspective
papers.key_contribution: Derives five design considerations for DPP systems from a structured literature review and systems-engineering principles, linking the system's purpose to concrete design options.
papers.classification_scheme: Five design considerations: strategic alignment with organizational goals; data requirements for decision making; system requirements for interoperability; tailoring to different circular practices; levers for value-chain collaboration.
papers.conformance_relevance: The interoperability system requirements are the only part a black-box engine can test. The rest is organizational. Existing check: none direct; manual.review for strategy items. New capability: none.

papers.title: Towards a Digital Product Passport Fit for Contributing to a Circular Economy
papers.key_contribution: An early actor-centred analysis of design options for the DPP, based on desk research and a stakeholder workshop. It asks who compiles data, in which data collection tool, and who may see it.
papers.classification_scheme: Actor-centred analysis: design options are examined per stakeholder group in a product value chain, against the existing regime of regulated and voluntary product information tools. No numbered classes in the abstract.
papers.conformance_relevance: Historic baseline for the stakeholder and role set. Useful for the role list in an access policy. Existing check: access.restricted_fields. New capability: none.

papers.title: Enhancing trust in global supply chains: Conceptualizing Digital Product Passports for a low-carbon hydrogen market
papers.key_contribution: Design principles for a DPP that verifies a product carbon footprint, derived from a structured review, expert interviews, and content analysis in the hydrogen supply chain.
papers.classification_scheme: Four design principles: collect data comprehensively and automatically; process it in a decentralized and tamper-proof way; protect stakeholder privacy and sovereignty; ensure interoperability.
papers.conformance_relevance: Tamper-evidence and privacy principles map to integrity.jws and access.restricted_fields. Decentralized processing has no check. Existing checks: integrity.jws, access.restricted_fields. New capability: ledger or anchor proof verification.
papers.notes: Crossref spells the first author Heß; Consensus spells Heeß.

papers.title: Blockchain-based digital product passport: design principles and demonstration
papers.key_contribution: Two years of design science research that yield an end-to-end blockchain-based DPP prototype in the textile industry and eleven design principles for such systems. It separates upstream transformation traceability from downstream event access.
papers.classification_scheme: Eleven design principles for blockchain-based DPPs (the abstract does not list them); information flow split into upstream production traceability and downstream lifecycle events.
papers.conformance_relevance: Representative of the DLT-anchored family. The engine cannot judge an on-chain record today. What it can test is the off-chain view: resolution, signature, version history. Existing checks: identifier.resolve, integrity.jws, persistence.versions. New capability: offline verification of an anchor or inclusion proof against a supplied proof file.

papers.title: Stop Guessing in the Dark: Identified Requirements for Digital Product Passport Systems
papers.key_contribution: Collects requirements for the DPP system (the infrastructure, not the data content) from stakeholder involvement plus science and industry literature. It composes, categorizes, and critically analyzes the list to find gaps.
papers.classification_scheme: A categorized requirement catalogue built from stakeholders and literature, with a gap analysis. The abstract names no categories and the full text could not be read (MDPI returns 403; the Wuppertal repository copy is behind bot protection).
papers.conformance_relevance: The closest thing to a requirement catalogue for DPP systems. Each requirement could become a test purpose with a status of placeholder until reviewed. Existing checks: depend on the requirement (not read). New capability: none; the catalogue must be read by a human with access to the full text before use.
papers.notes: OA URL per OpenAlex, not fetched. OpenAlex authors: Jansen, Meisen, Plociennik, Berg, Pomp, Windholz. Repository copy: https://epub.wupperinst.org/files/8135/8135_Jansen.pdf (blocked by Anubis at fetch time).

papers.title: A proposed universal definition of a Digital Product Passport Ecosystem (DPPE): Worldviews, discrete capabilities, stakeholder requirements and concerns
papers.key_contribution: Models the DPP ecosystem as a system of systems with a systems-engineering method, using the European Commission's open consultation on the Sustainable Products Initiative. It identifies nine high-level capabilities and maps information requirements to each.
papers.classification_scheme: Nine high-level capabilities of a DPP ecosystem, each linked to information requirements raised by stakeholder groups in the consultation. The capability names are not in the abstract.
papers.conformance_relevance: A capability list grounded in a public EU consultation. Could be the top level of a requirement tree. Existing check: none. New capability: none.
papers.notes: Crossref issue year is 2023; Consensus reports 2022 (probably the online date). Crossref gave a truncated title in the tool answer; the full title above is from Consensus and matches the DOI.

papers.title: Requirements for a Digital Product Passport to Boost the Circular Economy
papers.venue: Conference paper in a repository record (TUbilio, Technical University of Darmstadt per OpenAlex); the DOI prefix suggests the GI INFORMATIK 2022 volume, not verified
papers.key_contribution: Collects requirements for the DPP from several perspectives so that it is broadly applicable, because most early DPPs were sector-specific and no common standard existed.
papers.classification_scheme: Requirements grouped by stakeholder perspective. Classes were not read.
papers.conformance_relevance: Predecessor of Jansen et al. (shared authors). Use as a cross-check of that catalogue. Existing check: none. New capability: none.
papers.notes: Crossref returned HTTP 404; OpenAlex lists 13 authors starting with Plociennik.

papers.title: Bringing the Digital Product Passport to Life: Requirements Analysis for a Carbon Footprint Tracking System using Knowledge Graphs and Data Spaces
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 40th ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing
papers.key_contribution: Analyses what a DPP system must satisfy for carbon footprint tracking and discusses combining knowledge graphs with data spaces. It argues that DPP technology must be affordable and must not become a market entry barrier.
papers.classification_scheme: Requirement analysis for a carbon-footprint use case; no named classes in the abstract.
papers.conformance_relevance: Marks data-space and knowledge-graph systems as a distinct family. The engine has no check for either. Existing checks: data.context (JSON-LD context allowlist) for a part. New capabilities: data.shacl (interface_only) and a data-space connector probe.

papers.title: Ontology Requirements for Digital Product Passports based on the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation
papers.key_contribution: States requirements for an upper-level core ontology for DPPs and analyses key notions using only the text of the Ecodesign Regulation, so that semantic interoperability between DPP systems becomes possible.
papers.classification_scheme: Requirement set for a core ontology plus a list of key notions drawn from the regulation. Not read in detail.
papers.conformance_relevance: Supports a vocabulary-level check: terms in a passport map to a core ontology. Existing check: data.context only checks context URLs. New capability: data.shacl with pinned shapes.

papers.title: Methodology for defining data requirements for the Digital Product Passport under the ESPR framework
papers.key_contribution: A step-by-step method for deciding which data belong in a DPP and for justifying each inclusion. It turns policy goals and use cases into structured needs, tiers them as essential, strongly recommended or voluntary, and tests feasibility against industry practice. System design is covered only where it affects access rights, governance, or granularity.
papers.classification_scheme: Three requirement tiers: essential, strongly recommended, voluntary. Inputs: policy goals, use cases, industry data practice. Granularity and access rights are the system-design topics it covers.
papers.conformance_relevance: The three tiers give the engine a defensible way to weight data.rules findings (fail for essential, warn for the others). Existing check: data.rules (completeness rule packs). New capability: none; a rule-pack field for tier would be a catalogue change.
papers.notes: Summary is from the OpenAlex abstract. Publisher page not opened.

papers.title: A Reference Architecture for Digital Product Passports at Batch Level to Support Manufacturing Supply Chains
papers.venue: Research Challenges in Information Science (RCIS 2024), Lecture Notes in Business Information Processing 513
papers.key_contribution: A reference architecture for a manufacturer's DPP built on existing ERP, MES, and warehouse systems, with batch-level links between components and products. A Python and SQL proof of concept and a seven-person expert panel (Likert survey) were the validation.
papers.classification_scheme: (a) Data classes by source and change rate: static data read directly from one source; static data aggregated from several sources; dynamic data from one or more sources. (b) Granularity levels: product model, batch, item. (c) Four capability layers: data acquisition, data exchange, data processing, data access. (d) Gaps: granularity mismatch across the lifecycle, limited batch tracking, missing product data. (e) Design principles: standardized REST APIs with JSON-LD payloads, AAS-based data models, microservices, event-driven design, role-based access control, reuse of the ERP serial number for the carrier, automated product-to-batch link.
papers.conformance_relevance: Static and dynamic data classes and the three granularity levels give a clean test matrix: item-level GS1 forms are parseable today, batch (lot) forms are not. Existing checks: identifier.parse (item form only), api.contract, data.jsonschema, aas.validate, access.restricted_fields, persistence.versions. New capability: extend identifier.parse for batch and model-level GS1 Digital Link forms (a change in the identifier adapter contract).
papers.notes: Full text read from the University of Twente repository copy (OpenAlex marks it OA). Authors: Wiesner, Moreira, Guizzardi, Scholz. Proof-of-concept source reference given in the paper: a public GitHub repository (not opened).

papers.title: Towards a reference architecture for digital product passports in engineering
papers.key_contribution: An industry-neutral reference architecture derived from regulation and practice and checked on three use cases. The authors state that validation is incomplete and that scaling, cost, and cross-company data quality are open.
papers.classification_scheme: Five layers plus two cross-cutting axes. Layers: data (industry-neutral model of identity, bill of materials, composition, manufacturing and test parameters, usage events, certificates, environmental metrics, end-of-life data); communication (a seven-layer stack: data sources, integrity and provenance, unique identifiers and links, secure transport, access control, format and schema standardization, applications); architecture (front end with search, identifier resolution, dashboards; back end with access management, repository, compliance engine, engineering connector, monitoring, notifications, API gateway); function (mandatory: identification, versioning, security, governance, interoperability; optional: discovery, analytics, footprint calculation, onboarding); potential (engineering use cases). Axes: lifecycle phase and granularity from material to ecosystem.
papers.conformance_relevance: The seven-layer communication stack lists exactly the evidence classes an engine can observe (identifier link, schema, integrity, access). Existing checks: identifier.resolve, data.jsonschema, integrity.jws, access.restricted_fields, api.contract. The paper also names a compliance engine as a back-end component, which suggests where a vendor might expose a conformance hook; no existing check. New capability: none beyond those already interface_only.
papers.notes: Full text visible at the Cambridge page (open access, CC BY-NC-ND per the page). Paper cites AAS and GS1 only as examples.

papers.title: Architecture for a Digital Product Passport System based on the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation and the corresponding Standardisation Request
papers.key_contribution: Proposes a three-part DPP system architecture aligned with the Ecodesign Regulation and the Commission's standardisation request: central services run by the Commission for governance, distributed DPP system services run by economic operators or designated providers for daily operation, and third-party services that add functions.
papers.classification_scheme: Three service classes by operator: (1) central services (Commission), (2) DPP system services (economic operators or their providers), (3) third-party services. Authors per OpenAlex: Gering, Knothe, Böge, Fox, van Deventer, D'Agostino.
papers.conformance_relevance: Defines the actors a conformance test must separate: the engine tests a DPP system service from outside and needs mock central services and mock third parties. Existing checks: registry.consistency (mock registry only), api.contract. New capability: registry.official (interface_only) and further central-service emulation.
papers.found_via: consensus (title match without DOI or abstract); openalex (DOI and abstract)
papers.notes: Starting point named in the task. Consensus returned no DOI, no venue, and no abstract. DOI and abstract came from an OpenAlex title search. Crossref was not used (DataCite-style DOI). The Fraunhofer record page returned an Access Denied bot-protection page, so the full text was not read. The paper builds on a public EU request, not on the text of a CEN standard; none of that text is recorded here.

papers.title: Bridging the Gaps Towards a Unified Architecture for Digital Product Passports: A Data Space Perspective on Existing Standards and Initiatives
papers.key_contribution: A layered blueprint that stacks four existing building blocks: data spaces for governance and infrastructure (connectors, identity and trust, federated catalogs, policy-based contracts), AAS for structuring product data, CIRPASS semantic models for shared vocabularies, and GS1 for identification and event semantics.
papers.classification_scheme: Four-block layered stack: governance and infrastructure (data space), product data structure (AAS), semantics (CIRPASS vocabularies), identification and events (GS1). Data-space components named: connectors, identity and trust mechanisms, federated catalogs, policy-based contracts.
papers.conformance_relevance: Shows how several families combine, so an ICS must allow more than one family per system (hybrid). Existing checks cover the AAS block (aas.validate), identification block (identifier.parse, identifier.resolve), and partly semantics (data.context). No existing check covers connectors, catalogs, or contract negotiation. New capability: data-space connector probe against loopback fixtures.

papers.title: From Product Data to Circular Infrastructure: A System-of-Systems Analysis of Digital Product Passports Ecosystem
papers.venue: 2026 21st Annual System of Systems Engineering Conference (SoSE)
papers.key_contribution: Views the DPP ecosystem as a system of systems and proposes a multi-layer interoperability architecture. Design principles named: federated autonomy, modularity, interoperability first.
papers.classification_scheme: Four interoperability layers: technical, syntactic, semantic, governance. Design principles: federated autonomy, modularity, interoperability-first architecture.
papers.conformance_relevance: The four layers can index findings in a conformance report: transport and API (api.contract), syntax (data.jsonschema), semantics (data.context, data.shacl interface_only), governance (manual.review). Existing checks as listed. New capability: data.shacl for the semantic layer.

papers.title: From Static Records to Smart Passports: Evolving Digital Product Passports Toward Product-Service System Integration
papers.venue: 2025 21st International Conference on Distributed Computing in Smart Systems and the Internet of Things (DCOSS-IoT)
papers.key_contribution: A state-of-the-art review of DPP frameworks and EU projects that finds limits in service integration, real-time synchronization, modularity, and stakeholder trust. It proposes DPSSP4.0, a service-aware passport architecture built on AAS, microservices, semantic data spaces, and certification layers.
papers.classification_scheme: Limitation classes found in current architectures: service integration, real-time data synchronization, modularity, stakeholder trust. Proposed layers: AAS core, microservices, semantic data space, certification layer.
papers.conformance_relevance: The certification layer is a place where conformance evidence could be attached to a passport. Existing check: aas.validate for the AAS core. New capability: evidence.untp_dcc (interface_only) if a conformity credential is the carrier of that evidence.

papers.title: Digital Product Passports: Use Cases Framework and Technical Architecture Using DLT and Smart Contracts
papers.venue: 2023 19th International Conference on Distributed Computing in Smart Systems and the Internet of Things (DCOSS-IoT)
papers.key_contribution: A use-case framework of nested passports along lifecycle stages and a reference architecture that sends IoT sensor data through a gateway to smart contracts on a DAG-based ledger (IOTA), with a Python back end and cache in front. A prototype is public; performance evaluation is left to future work.
papers.classification_scheme: Use-case reference framework: lifecycle stages raw material, material, product, final product, consumption, new life; passports nest from material to product and are visible by access layer. Nine design goals borrowed from digital-twin work: controllable, decentral, private, secure, discoverable, interoperable, portable, simple, extensible. Seven content areas: unique identifier, product information and instructions, maintenance and disassembly, carbon footprint, recycling, certificates and standards, legislation compliance. Smart-contract methods: generate identifier, update (append a new version), migrate or merge passports, read history, first version, latest version.
papers.conformance_relevance: The append-only version array with first, latest, and history reads is a concrete update rule that persistence.versions can test from outside. Passport nesting means a conformance run must follow links between passports. Existing checks: persistence.versions, identifier.consistency. New capability: link-following across nested passports with a bound on depth.
papers.notes: Full text read (all 7 pages) from the Bournemouth repository copy. Evaluation is deferred: the authors state that TPS and confirmation-failure rates are future work.

papers.title: From Regulation to Realisation: Architecting a Digital Battery Passport System
papers.venue: 2025 IEEE International Symposium on Systems Engineering (ISSE)
papers.key_contribution: A multi-level systems architecture for a battery-passport reporting tool aimed at SMEs, refined over two abstraction levels with a Delphi panel. It turns regulatory and operational requirements into functional components.
papers.classification_scheme: Two abstraction levels of functional components derived from Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 requirements; Delphi rounds for validation. Components not listed in the abstract.
papers.conformance_relevance: Shows that regulation text is turned into functional components by hand. Engine rule packs for batteries should cite Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 articles and annexes, not a standard. Existing check: data.rules. New capability: none.

papers.title: Digital Product Passport Design Supporting the Circular Economy Based on the Asset Administration Shell
papers.key_contribution: Consolidates standards and literature into a DPP data model built on the Asset Administration Shell, mapping data requirements to submodel templates and filling the gaps. It states that the model fits the battery passport and stays cross-industry.
papers.classification_scheme: Mapping of DPP data requirements to AAS submodel templates, with a list of gaps where no template exists. Classes not read.
papers.conformance_relevance: Directly relevant to aas.validate. A valid AAS is not a complete DPP statement, so the engine needs a DPP submodel-template check on top. Existing check: aas.validate (experimental). New capability: a pinned-template submodel check built from IDTA specifications only.
papers.notes: MDPI blocks WebFetch; abstract only. SciSpace lists the first author as M. Kuhn.

papers.title: Digital Product Passport as a Digital Twin? Analyzing Conceptual Intersections and Deriving Design Elements
papers.key_contribution: Studies the relationship between digital twins and DPPs, applies a multidimensional digital-twin characterization to place a DT-based DPP, and derives design elements. It concludes that DPPs can act as standardized, verified data layers inside DT ecosystems.
papers.classification_scheme: Multidimensional digital-twin characterization applied to DPPs. Derived design elements: data structures, access rights, interoperability, identifiers, storage, data carriers.
papers.conformance_relevance: Answers the question on digital twin versus DPP: the DPP is a verified data layer, so an AAS-based DT does not by itself satisfy a DPP claim. Supports keeping aas.validate as a partial check. The six design elements match the engine's check families. Existing checks: aas.validate and those for each element. New capability: none.

papers.title: A Digital Twin-Based Digital Product Passport
papers.key_contribution: A design science study that builds a digital-twin-based DPP architecture and a prototype for certified geo-food products, with a formative evaluation by expert interviews. It adds social and economic data to the usual environmental focus.
papers.classification_scheme: Not a classification; one architecture and one prototype. Evaluation was qualitative.
papers.conformance_relevance: Example of a sector pilot that evaluates by interview only, which the engine would classify as manual evidence. Existing check: manual.review. New capability: none.

papers.title: Digital Product Passport Management with Decentralised Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials
papers.key_contribution: Reads the Ecodesign Regulation's passport articles into nine system requirements and shows how decentralised identifiers (DIDs), verifiable credentials (VCs) and verifiable presentations could meet them. The DPP becomes a collection of credentials plus an optional DID per product, with selective disclosure per requesting role, and a chain of related credentials is proposed against fraud. Performance sections (pages 15 onward) were not read.
papers.classification_scheme: Nine requirements R-01 to R-09: R-01 product identifiers (a global trade item number stays the product key; a DID may complement it); R-02 model, batch or item granularity fixed by each product-group act; R-03 maintenance of the passport along the life cycle (who keeps it as ownership changes); R-04 availability for the period set by the act, even after the maker ceases to exist; R-05 only named actors create or update data; R-06 access by role; R-07 authentication, reliability and integrity of data; R-08 security, privacy and fraud avoidance; R-09 negligible burden on operators. Design alternatives per requirement: identifier options D01.1 to D01.3 (DID with ISO identifier side by side, ISO identifier inside the DID, ISO identifier only); storage options D02.1 to D02.3 (registry, DID document, credentials per component); lifecycle options D03.1 to D03.3 (no action, change DID controller, transfer credentials); fraud option D08.1 (chain of related credentials, one per lifecycle transition). Architecture roles: issuer, holder (wallet), verifier, verifiable data registry. The authors note that wallet interaction protocols are not fixed by the W3C model, so several exist.
papers.conformance_relevance: Provides a requirement-to-mechanism table for the VC and SSI family. Legal anchors (Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 9(2)(d), (f), (g), (i); Art. 11(e), (f), (g), (h)) were re-read in the consolidated text. The engine verifies JWS today; credential proofs, DID resolution, status lists, and chain-of-credential checks are missing. A conformance test can walk the credential chain and check that each transition has a valid signature from a trusted issuer. Existing check: integrity.jws (single token). New capability: integrity.status_list (interface_only), a DID resolver fed by local fixtures, credential and presentation verification, chain-of-credentials walk.
papers.notes: Preprint (extended version). Pages 1 to 14 of the arXiv PDF were read; Crossref was not used (arXiv DataCite DOI). The paper cites Art. 9(2)(h) for the availability period, while the consolidated regulation text places that duty in Art. 9(2)(i); recorded as a citation slip in the paper. The paper also mentions standard numbers from Annex III of the regulation; no standard content is recorded here.

papers.title: Enhancing Digital Product Passports with Material Fingerprinting and Decentralized Non-Conformity Signals: Application to Critical Raw Materials
papers.key_contribution: System architecture and data model from the Ma-DiTraCe project: self-sovereign identity and verifiable credentials with an optional blockchain anchoring layer. Material fingerprints from chemical, isotopic or spectral analysis are signed as credentials to tie physical material to the digital record, and aggregated non-conformity signals support live certification management.
papers.classification_scheme: Two differentiators named: physical-to-digital binding through signed fingerprint credentials; decentralized red-flag governance. Layers: SSI and VC core, optional ledger anchoring.
papers.conformance_relevance: Physical authenticity binding is outside what digital consistency can show, so the engine must keep its current disclaimer. Fingerprint credentials need credential verification and status checks. Existing check: integrity.jws. New capability: VC verification and integrity.status_list.

papers.title: A Design Study on Integrating UNTP Semantics into AAS Submodels for Digital Product Passports
papers.key_contribution: Proposes embedding UN/CEFACT Transparency Protocol DPP semantics as an AAS submodel, so that one technical vehicle carries a sector-neutral semantic base. It discusses data-space integration, other standards, and the limited maturity of UNTP, and states that empirical validation is still needed.
papers.classification_scheme: Layering of semantic base (UNTP), technical vehicle (AAS), and sector ecosystems as downstream applications.
papers.conformance_relevance: Shows that two families (UNTP credentials and AAS) are being merged, so a UNTP document could appear inside an AAS file. Existing checks: aas.validate, data.jsonschema (with a pinned UNTP schema). New capability: evidence.untp_dcc and a pinned UNTP version (interface_only; needs a maintainer decision).

papers.title: Made2Verify: A Scalable GS1-Compliant Resolver and Fallback Dashboard for Digital Product Passports
papers.key_contribution: A resolver and fallback dashboard that sits between QR or NFC identifiers and DPP data repositories. It redirects by lifecycle stage, authentication needs, and endpoint availability, and keeps essential data reachable when a manufacturer ceases operation. It was tried on a remanufacture part in a lab and a production setting.
papers.classification_scheme: Redirection behaviours: lifecycle-aware routing and fallback on operator discontinuity. Carrier input: QR code, NFC tag.
papers.conformance_relevance: Gives concrete failure modes for identifier.resolve: wrong redirect for a lifecycle stage, dead endpoint without fallback. Persistence after the operator is gone cannot be proved by a single run. Existing checks: identifier.resolve, identifier.consistency, persistence.versions. New capability: persistence.scheduled (interface_only) with recorded acquisitions at intervals.

papers.title: From Tag to Digital Twin: Unlocking Service Resolution Through GS1 Digital Link
papers.venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on RFID Technology and Applications (RFID-TA)
papers.key_contribution: Design and implementation of a GS1-conformant resolver with a mobile app that scans Digital Link identifiers on QR, NFC, RFID, Wi-Fi access point, and Bluetooth carriers. It is deployed in port-to-port supply chains and in DPPs and returns requester-specific information through one URL.
papers.classification_scheme: Carrier modalities supported by one resolver: QR code, NFC, RFID, Wi-Fi access point, Bluetooth.
papers.conformance_relevance: Evidence that one identifier can reach several carriers and that responses depend on the requester. Existing checks: carrier.qr_decode, identifier.resolve. New capability: carrier.nfc, carrier.rfid (interface_only); requester-specific resolution needs roles on the resolve path.

papers.title: Building Digital Product Passports: EPCIS 2.0 Meets Knowledge Graphs
papers.key_contribution: An architecture that ingests EPCIS 2.0 visibility events from distributed sources and links them through GS1 keys into a knowledge graph, so that a full product history needs one query even after transformations and aggregations.
papers.classification_scheme: Event-based traceability layer plus graph layer; no classes beyond that.
papers.conformance_relevance: Represents the EPCIS family. The engine has no EPCIS check. A pinned JSON Schema could validate event documents. Existing check: data.jsonschema (partial). New capability: EPCIS capture and query interface probe on a loopback fixture, and key-link consistency across events.

papers.title: A DLT- and ZKP-Enabled Framework for Privacy-Preserving Digital Product Passports in Maritime Container Logistics
papers.key_contribution: Ocean DPP: a platform combining EPCIS 2.0, oneM2M, IOTA, and Groth16 zero-knowledge proofs so that stakeholders can verify compliance predicates without seeing raw sensor values, with Merkle batching to cut anchoring cost. It reports 16 experiments on one host with synthetic load, 100 percent EPCIS 2.0 compliance, and no permanent message loss in four failure-injection scenarios.
papers.classification_scheme: Layers: event capture (EPCIS 2.0), device layer (oneM2M), ledger anchoring (IOTA with Merkle batching), privacy proofs (zero-knowledge). Evaluation scenarios: latency, throughput, proof time, failure injection.
papers.conformance_relevance: One of the few papers that reports a compliance figure and failure injection against its own platform, but on a single host and synthetic data. Existing checks: none for EPCIS or proofs. New capability: EPCIS interface probe and offline verification of a Merkle inclusion proof or ZKP against supplied test vectors.
papers.notes: The 100 percent figure is the authors' own and is not independently verified here.

papers.title: Towards a Modular Testing Environment for Digital Battery Passports
papers.key_contribution: A position paper that argues for a freely available test environment where battery distributors can verify that their data, interfaces and system functions conform to regulatory and technical requirements. It outlines modular test procedures, emulation of central components, validation of data structures, interaction protocols and security mechanisms, plus the process models and test types required.
papers.classification_scheme: Test environment functions: definition and execution of modular test procedures; emulation of central components; validation of data structures, interaction protocols, and security mechanisms. Test types and process models are mentioned in the abstract but not listed.
papers.conformance_relevance: The only paper in the corpus about conformance testing of DPP systems, and it matches the engine's plan: modular test packs, mock central components (registry.mock), and checks for data, interface, and security. Existing checks: data.jsonschema, api.contract, integrity.jws, registry.consistency. New capability: broader central-component emulation. The test-type list needs the full text.
papers.notes: OpenAlex marks it open access and lists a Fraunhofer-Publica copy (publica/518049). ScienceDirect returned 403 and the Fraunhofer page is behind bot protection, so only the abstract was read.

papers.title: Explainability-Oriented Semantic Validation for Digital Product Passports in Industrial Systems
papers.venue: 2026 1st International Conference on Human Centric Artificial Intelligence (ICHCAI)
papers.key_contribution: A layered architecture that keeps conceptual alignment, executable SHACL validation, and explanation generation as separate assets, with an explanation model that turns each SHACL finding into violation, interpretation, impact, and recommended action. A rule-based analysis of two public CIRPASS datasets shows that identifier declaration, access-control specification, storage strategy, interoperability, and security are covered unevenly across initiatives.
papers.classification_scheme: Validation dimensions derived from a public standards dataset: identifier declaration, access-control specification, storage strategy, interoperability, security. Explanation model fields: violation, interpretation, operational impact, recommended action.
papers.conformance_relevance: Directly shows how SHACL results can be reported in a decision-relevant form, which fits the engine's reason codes. The five dimensions are a ready list of what an initiative should declare in an ICS. Existing check: data.rules (partial). New capability: data.shacl (interface_only) with pinned local shapes.
papers.notes: Uses CIRPASS project datasets that include a standards dataset; the standards' content is not recorded here.

papers.title: Digital Passport Model Assessment Workbench: SHACL-based assessment, use-case coverage, and integration guidance for digital passport model ecosystems
papers.key_contribution: An open-source tool (Python package, also a containerised MCP server) that computes deterministic assessment metrics directly from SHACL model specifications: structural scale, typed and cardinality-bounded properties, constraint density, cross-module references, use-case coverage, and composition advice. The demonstration compares the CE-RISE model ecosystem with the BatteryPass v1.2.0 model ecosystem and finds 14 strict overlap pairs.
papers.classification_scheme: Assessment metrics grouped as structure, constraint readiness, interoperability, use-case coverage, integration risk.
papers.conformance_relevance: A deterministic, model-level assessment that needs no instance data, which fits the engine's no-language-model rule. It evaluates models, not running systems. Existing check: data.jsonschema (analogous for JSON). New capability: data.shacl (interface_only); the tool itself is a candidate dependency to report, not to add.
papers.notes: Dependency note for the owner: any use of this package needs an explicit dependency approval (repository rule 10).

papers.title: Compliance-by-Design: Validating Decentralised Architectures for Digital Product Passports under the EU Data Governance Act
papers.venue: 2025 21st International Conference on Network and Service Management (CNSM)
papers.key_contribution: Assesses a decentralised DPP architecture (data intermediaries, decentralised identity, cryptography) against the Data Governance Act, with GDPR and the Ecodesign Regulation as complements. Early pilots in two projects are used as evidence for neutrality, structural separation, fair access, registration, and confidentiality.
papers.classification_scheme: Requirement list drawn from the Data Governance Act: neutrality, structural separation, fair access, registration, confidentiality; validation by pilot.
papers.conformance_relevance: An example of validating an architecture against public EU law instead of a standard, which is the pattern the engine must follow. Most items are organizational. Existing checks: access.restricted_fields for confidentiality; manual.review for registration and neutrality. New capability: none.

conformance_implications.implication: Carrier classes in the literature are QR code, NFC, RFID (and serial-number or barcode forms). The engine decodes QR images only.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: carrier.nfc and carrier.rfid reader integrations (interface_only today) with a tag campaign; decoder for other 2D carrier forms is not registered.

conformance_implications.legal_anchor: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 9(2)(d) and Art. 10(1)(f): the product-group act decides model, batch, or item level.
conformance_implications.implication: Granularity is model, batch, or item. The identifier parser accepts only the item form /01/<GTIN>/21/<serial>.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: Extend identifier.parse to further GS1 Digital Link forms (GTIN only, lot-level qualifiers, path prefix) pinned to the open GS1 specifications. This changes the identifier adapter contract.

conformance_implications.legal_anchor: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1)(a) (persistent unique identifier through a data carrier), Art. 10(4) (back-up copy at a service provider), Art. 11(e) (availability for the set period, also after insolvency, liquidation, or cessation of activity of the responsible operator).
conformance_implications.implication: Resolvers redirect by lifecycle stage and requester, and a fallback must keep data reachable after an operator stops. A single run cannot prove persistence.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: persistence.scheduled (interface_only) with recorded acquisitions at intervals; redirect-chain and link-type checks.

conformance_implications.legal_anchor: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1)(d) (open standards, interoperable format, transfer through an open data exchange network without vendor lock-in), Art. 11(a) (full interoperability on technical, semantic, and organisational aspects), Art. 11(c) (storage by the responsible operator or by service providers).
conformance_implications.implication: Distributed DPP system services have an interface that others call; the service split (central, operator, third party) is the basis for black-box testing.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: api.fuzz (interface_only; needs a signed authorization scope); pinned contracts per system.

conformance_implications.legal_anchor: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1)(d) (machine-readable, structured, searchable data) and Art. 9(2)(a) with Annex III (data to include).
conformance_implications.implication: Data validation appears in three forms: JSON Schema, JSON-LD vocabulary control, and SHACL on linked data. Tiering data elements as essential, strongly recommended, or voluntary supports weighted findings.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: data.shacl (interface_only) with pinned local shapes; a tier field in rule packs.

conformance_implications.implication: AAS-based passports are common, but a valid AAS is not a complete DPP statement; a DPP is a verified data layer inside a twin.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: A submodel-template check against pinned IDTA templates; pinned UNTP schema if UNTP is embedded.

conformance_implications.legal_anchor: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 9(2)(f) (which actors access which data), Art. 10(1)(g) and Art. 11(b) (access by named actor groups according to access rights set in the delegated act), Art. 11(f) (update rights restricted by those access rights).
conformance_implications.implication: Role-based access, selective disclosure, and granular access management are named as open needs.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: none for role views on fetch; selective disclosure of credentials needs VC verification.

conformance_implications.legal_anchor: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 11(g) (data authentication, reliability, and integrity) and Art. 11(h) (security, privacy, fraud avoided).
conformance_implications.implication: Trust is delivered by signatures today and by credentials and decentralised identifiers in the SSI family.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: integrity.cose and integrity.status_list (interface_only); DID resolution with local fixtures; VC proof verification.

conformance_implications.implication: Ledger-anchored systems expose an append-only version history; the on-chain part cannot be judged from outside without a proof.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: Offline verification of an inclusion or anchor proof supplied by the system under test; no live node.

conformance_implications.implication: Event-based traceability with EPCIS 2.0 is a distinct family with its own capture and query interfaces.
conformance_implications.existing_check: data.jsonschema (partial, with a pinned EPCIS schema)
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: EPCIS capture and query interface probe on loopback fixtures; link consistency across events.

conformance_implications.implication: Data-space and federated systems depend on connectors, catalogs, identity, and policy contracts; sovereignty is a main requirement.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: Data-space connector probe (catalog, contract negotiation) against loopback fixtures with pinned identity anchors.

conformance_implications.implication: Central services (registry, authority) and third-party services must be emulated to test a DPP system service in isolation.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: registry.official (interface_only) and a wider set of emulated central components.

conformance_implications.legal_anchor: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 9(1) (data accurate, complete, up to date), Art. 9(2)(g) and (h) (who may create or update, and the update arrangements), Art. 11(d) (a new passport for a product that already has one must be linked to the original).
conformance_implications.implication: Static data versus dynamic data, and the use-phase update path for third parties, are a recurring design dimension.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: An authorized active write-path test; the engine has no write check today.

conformance_implications.implication: Organizational maturity, governance, and strategy claims cannot be seen from outside.
Reviews report little real-system validation and no cross-organizational testing; the engine's recorded black-box runs address that gap and can label evidence with a validation-maturity scale.

cross_paper_observations: No single accepted classification exists. Five kinds appear: (a) attribute grids built by reviews (Psarommatis, 20+ attributes; Wan, four areas), (b) a morphological taxonomy (Shamsir, Paeplow and Möller: 21 dimensions in four meta-dimensions), (c) design-space dimensions (Käser: three), (d) layered or service-split reference architectures (Trienens five layers and two axes; Wiesner four capability layers; Gering three service classes; Kranner four-block stack; Behdani four interoperability layers), and (e) requirement or design-principle lists (Nowacki nine goals; Heß four; Abreu eleven; Christensen five).

The same dimensions recur under different names: identification and data carrier; where the data live and who runs them (central or decentral); data model and semantics; identity and access control; integrity and trust (signatures, credentials, ledger); dynamic update and versioning; interoperability by layer; governance. These line up with the engine's check families, which supports a profile (ICS) with one block per dimension.

Blockchain is the most often proposed enabler in the reviews, yet the large review (Psarommatis) and several authors point to scalability, cost, and energy limits and to hybrid architectures in practice. The engine should treat ledger anchoring as optional evidence, not as a required component.

AAS and GS1 are the two standards named most often as common ground (Wiesner, Trienens, Kranner, Shamsir). UNTP and verifiable credentials are an emerging third (Havur, García, Abdallah). Data spaces are used where data sovereignty matters (Kranner, Belova, Fabianek).

Real-system validation is rare. Lyse and Psarommatis report that most work is conceptual, and validation is mostly case study, prototype, or interview. Where authors do test, it is a proof of concept with a small expert panel (Wiesner, seven experts), a single-host experiment with synthetic load (Khairy), or early pilots (Fabianek).

Only one paper addresses conformance testing of DPP systems directly (Gering and Knothe, test environment for battery passports) and it is a position paper. Two others offer deterministic validation of data models with SHACL (Samarathunga, Boero); they check models, not running systems.

Digital twin versus DPP: the corpus treats the DPP as a verified, standardized data layer that a twin (often AAS) can host (Ebel), and design goals for DPPs are borrowed from twin research (Nowacki). A valid AAS file therefore does not prove a DPP claim, in line with the engine's own aas.validate note.

Granularity (model, batch, item) and static versus dynamic data are explicit design choices (Wiesner). The engine's identifier.parse handles item-level GS1 Digital Link only, so batch and model-level systems cannot be tested end to end today.

Requirement sources split in two. Public EU-law sources (JRC method report, Ecodesign Regulation, Regulation (EU) 2023/1542) give data content and tiers. Stakeholder studies (Jansen, Plociennik, King) give system requirements. Standards-derived requirements are not recorded here by rule.

García et al. is the only paper that turns the passport articles of the Ecodesign Regulation into a numbered list of system requirements (R-01 to R-09: identifier, granularity, lifecycle maintenance, availability, creation and update rights, role-based access, integrity, security and fraud, low burden). Each maps to an article that was re-read in the consolidated text. This list is a good seed for engine test purposes with a legal anchor, with one correction: availability is Art. 9(2)(i), not (h).

No recorded paper takes the platform or SaaS approach as its own architecture class. Vendor platforms appear only as the service-provider actor type in the Shamsir et al. taxonomy. The platform-saas family therefore has to be described from vendor and project sources in other research tasks, not from this literature set.

Most items are recent: of 45 recorded papers, 32 are from 2025 or 2026, and many 2026 items are Procedia Computer Science conference papers from one conference series, so abstracts dominate what can be read. Reviews published in the same period overlap heavily in what they cite.
